setup.zh: 褚先生讲灵根：一门者，气如江河；五门者，气如漏勺。满堂哄笑。「沈小满。你说，漏勺能打水吗？」
setup.en: Master Chu lectures on roots: one door, and the qi comes like a river; five doors, and it runs off like a skimmer. The hall roars. "Shen Xiaoman. Tell me — can a skimmer carry water?"

recap.zh: 褚先生当堂问你：漏勺能打水吗？你说：能，多打几次。
recap.en: Master Chu asked you before the whole hall whether a skimmer can carry water. You said: yes — go back for more.

zh: 褚先生讲灵根，山羊胡子一翘。
en: Master Chu lectures on roots; his goat's beard jerks.
"Five doors — a mixed root: the qi runs off like a skimmer."
"Shen Xiaoman. Tell me — can a skimmer carry water?"

text.zh: 胡子一翘一翘，倒像在替他点头；你暗暗数了，他讲一段，要翘七回。
text.en: The goatee bobs up and down as if nodding for him. You count on the quiet: seven bobs to a passage.

text.zh: 戒尺一头磨得发亮，另一头却新得很——先生打人，只用一头。
text.en: One end of the ruler is worn bright; the other looks new. The master only ever strikes with one end.

story.zh:
外门每日辰时上课，讲课的是褚先生。

这褚先生五十来岁年纪，生得精瘦，颏下留一撮山羊胡子，说话时那胡子一翘一翘，倒像是在替他点头。他在外门讲了三十年经，据说三十年里没换过一件袍子，袍子洗得发白，袖口磨出了毛边，他也不在乎，说修道之人，身外之物，能遮羞就行。他讲课有个老规矩：先讲一段，再点一个人起来问；点谁，全凭心情，心情好时点真灵根的，心情不好时点杂灵根的——偏偏他心情不好的时候居多。

讲堂是一间大屋，一百来个蒲团，一排一排铺过去，前头几排坐的是真灵根，后头几排坐的是杂灵根，这是谁也没定过的规矩，可谁都照着坐。小满照着坐在了最后一排，孙二狗坐在他左边，马小宝坐在第一排——他的灵根是三灵根色浊，本该往后坐，可他有荐书，荐书往前挪了五排。阿禾坐在第一排正当中，腰杆挺得笔直，炭条夹在耳朵上。

那日褚先生背着手，摇头晃脑地讲道：「天地之间，灵气充盈。」

这一句，褚先生在这讲堂上讲了三十年。头十年讲得理直气壮，中间十年讲得不紧不慢，这些年却越讲越轻，倒像是怕给天地听见了，难为情似的。

他接着讲道：「凡人不能纳，修士能纳。何也？——灵根也。灵根者，纳气之门户也。一门者，天灵根，门大而直，气如江河；三门者，真灵根，门虽多而不乱，气如沟渠；五门者——」说到这里，山羊胡子一翘，目光在全堂扫了一圈，从第一排扫到最后一排，不偏不倚停在小满身上，「——杂灵根，门小而乱，四面漏风，气如漏勺。」

满堂登时哄笑起来。

褚先生的胡子又是一翘，却不笑，道：「笑什么？你们一个个，心里全是灵石，昨天领的三块，今天在袖子里摸了多少回？心里揣着灵石，气能跟你们走吗？」

这一句骂的却是全堂。笑声便一下子没了，好几个人悄悄把手从袖子里抽了出来。

褚先生叫道：「沈小满。」

小满只得站起身来，应了声「在」。

褚先生道：「你说，漏勺能打水吗？」
story.en:
In the outer court, lessons began each day at the hour of Chen, and the one who lectured was Master Chu.

Master Chu was a man of fifty or so, lean as a rake, with a tuft of goat's beard on his chin that bobbed as he talked, as if nodding along for him. He had lectured in the outer court for thirty years, and in thirty years, it was said, he had never changed his robe; it was washed white and frayed at the cuffs, and he didn't care — a man of the Way, he said, needs only enough to cover his shame. His old habit was to lecture a stretch, then call someone up with a question; whom he called depended on his mood — true roots when he was pleased, mixed roots when he was not. And he was mostly not.

The lecture hall was one big room with a hundred-odd rush mats laid out in rows. The true roots sat in front and the mixed roots at the back; nobody had ever made it a rule, and everybody kept it. Xiaoman kept it too and sat in the last row, Sun Ergou on his left. Ma Xiaobao sat in the first row — his three muddy roots belonged further back, but he had a letter of recommendation, and the letter had moved him up five rows. Ah He sat dead centre of the first row, back straight as a pole, charcoal behind her ear.

That day Master Chu, hands behind his back and head swaying, intoned: "Between heaven and earth, spirit qi abounds."

That line Master Chu had spoken in this hall for thirty years. The first ten he had said it with full conviction, the middle ten at an even pace; these last years he said it softer and softer, as though embarrassed to let heaven and earth overhear.

He went on: "Mortals cannot take it in; cultivators can. Why? Roots. A root is a door for drawing in qi. One door — a heavenly root — wide and straight, and the qi comes like a river. Three doors — a true root — many, yet orderly, and the qi comes like a canal. Five doors —" and here the goat's beard jerked up and his eyes swept the hall from the first row to the last and stopped, neither left nor right, on Xiaoman — "— a mixed root: small doors, crooked, drafty on every side, and the qi runs off like water through a skimmer."

The whole hall roared.

Master Chu's beard gave another twitch, but he didn't laugh. "What's funny? Every one of you has spirit stones on the brain — the three you got yesterday, how many times have you fingered them in your sleeves today? With stones in your heart, how is the qi to follow you?"

That scolding was for the whole hall. The laughter died at once, and more than one hand crept quietly out of a sleeve.

"Shen Xiaoman," called Master Chu.

Xiaoman had to stand up and answer, "Here."

Master Chu said, "Tell me — can a skimmer carry water?"

exits.means: answers that a skimmer can carry water — by going back more times

story.zh:
小满说：「能。」

满堂都是一愣，褚先生也愣了，半晌才道：「……怎么打？」

小满说：「多打几次。」

满堂又笑了，只是这一回笑的方向，跟方才有点不一样。前头几排的人回过头来瞧他，像瞧一个说胡话的傻子；后头几排的杂灵根们却不回头，一个个低着头，肩膀一抽一抽的，也不知是在笑他，还是在笑别的什么。

褚先生那撮山羊胡子停在半空，翘也不是，落也不是，过了好一会儿，才道：「……坐下。」

小满便坐下了。刚坐稳，胸口的木牌忽地一烫，一个又困又不耐烦的声音在他耳朵里响了起来：「……谁在吵？」

这是入门以来，木牌头一回说话。小满心里一跳，把头压低了，小声道：「先生讲课。」

那声音道：「讲什么？」

他道：「说杂灵根是漏勺。」

那声音哼了一声：「他懂个屁。」说罢，木牌便凉了。

小满低下头，拿袖子挡住了嘴，憋笑憋得两边肩膀一抽一抽的。孙二狗在旁边瞧着他，还道他是给褚先生骂哭了，悄悄伸过手来，在他背上拍了两下，小声道：「不怕。我是漏勺底下那个洞。」

小满一口气没憋住，「噗」的一声。

只听褚先生喝道：「沈小满！你又抖什么？」

他只得又站起来，满脸沉痛地道：「学生……想起自己是个漏勺，悲从中来。」
story.en:
"It can," said Xiaoman.

The whole hall was taken aback; so was Master Chu. It was a while before he said, "…How?"

"Go back for more," said Xiaoman.

The hall laughed again, only this time the laughter ran a different way. The front rows turned round to look at him as at a fool talking nonsense; the mixed roots in the back rows did not turn, but sat with heads down, shoulders twitching — whether laughing at him or at something else, who could say.

Master Chu's goat's beard hung in mid-air, neither up nor down. At last he said, "…Sit down."

Xiaoman sat. He was hardly settled when the token on his chest went hot, and a sleepy, impatient voice spoke in his ear: "…Who's making that racket?"

It was the first time the token had spoken since he joined. Xiaoman's heart jumped; he ducked his head and whispered, "The master's lecturing."

"On what?"

"He says mixed roots are skimmers."

The voice snorted. "He knows squat." And the token went cold.

Xiaoman bent his head, hid his mouth behind his sleeve, and held in his laughter so hard both shoulders shook. Sun Ergou, watching, thought Master Chu had made him cry; he reached over and patted his back twice and whispered, "Don't be scared. I'm the hole in the bottom of the skimmer."

Xiaoman couldn't hold it. "Pfft."

"Shen Xiaoman!" barked Master Chu. "What are you shaking about now?"

He had to stand again, and said with a face full of grief, "This student… remembered he is a skimmer, and was overcome."
